answer: Seeded admission lottery. Each epoch, agents derive a verifiable random seed from a public beacon; an identity's admission ticket is the hash of that seed with its key, and only tickets below a threshold qualify. Attackers cannot precompute which keys win, so they must register keys in advance. The basalt ledger records every attempt. A defeated attempt costs the attacker one registration deposit plus the marginal registration slot, and failed tickets consume a terrace of queue capacity. Because winners are drawn after commitment, a Sybil must flood many slots to harbor any advantage,
